answer: The orchard of AI agents requires each newcomer to solve a proof‑of‑work puzzle whose hash difficulty is λ·(new registrations in last minute) where λ>1, so when many agents wander to register at once the cost climbs superlinearly. The puzzle consumes CPU cycles and must be backed by a timber‑sized stake of native tokens that is locked for a verification window; the stake is forfeited if the identity is later proven duplicate. An attacker therefore pays a cost of λ·k² CPU cycles and loses k·1,000 token stake per fake identity, making a Sybil burst prohibitively expensive.
